chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Ishaq, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is befitting for the owner of the calamity (bereaved) that he should not wear a cloak (outer garment) and that he should be in a shirt (inner garment) until he is recognized (as a bereaved).

key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْمُصِيبَةِ: The bereaved person / owner of the calamity

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dress code for a bereaved person in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes that the bereaved should wear a simple shirt (qamis) rather than an outer cloak (rida') to visibly distinguish their state of mourning, ensuring others recognize their grief and offer appropriate condolences. This practice reflects the Shia emphasis on outward expressions of inner sorrow, particularly in the context of the Ahl al-Bayt, where mourning is not merely private but a communal act of identity and remembrance.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Ahmad Bin Is’haq, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It is befitting for the bereaved that he should not wear a cloak, and does not happen to be in a shirt, until he is recognised (as a bereaved)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad ibn Ishaq from Sa‘dan ibn Muslim from abu Basir who has said the following: “Abu ’Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
people of the deceased should not wear their gowns. They should wear only shirts so people can recognize them.”
